problems: The blind guess (a stylised human figure) does not match the intended subject, a knot. The image reads clearly as a knot diagram with two rope tails and a bight.
The blue tubes mostly trace the gold lines closely, so the figure reads as a copy of the gold skeleton rather than an independent silhouette. The loops are thin and offset only slightly.

Star placement is broadly sensible: the eye of the hitch sits at the crossing near (250,224), the upper rope tip at (217,121), the long tail tip at top left, the right tail tip at (442,251), and the lower tail end at (408,470). The lower bight stars (around (138,380) and (285,358)) also sit on the bight.

Labels overlap each other and the drawing. 'left edge of the knot body' collides with 'upper left loop of the knot', 'the eye of the hitch, where' runs over the tail, and 'outer left edge of the lower bight' is cut off. Several labels are truncated at the right or bottom of the text.
Orientation is acceptable: the knot is upright with tails leaving downward and to the right, with no mirroring problem.
output.advice: Redraw so the figure reads as a knot silhouette rather than a human. Keep the star positions for the eye of the hitch, the upper rope tip, the long tail tip, the right tail tip, and the lower tail end. Give the knot body and bight thicker, filled or clearly closed blue tube loops that are offset from the gold lines, so they read as an independent silhouette. Make the two bight loops more distinct. Move labels into a clear margin with leader lines so none overlap or get clipped. Reduce gold line dominance so the blue mass carries the shape.
